angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 730,485 km at 349.77 pc = 0.03 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 2.8590 +/- 0.0154 mas (same row, RUWE 1.15): 349.77 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.05 +/- 0.05 solar radii from Hellier et al. 2014, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of WASP-96 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.440.1982H/abstract): 730,485 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.06 +/- 0.09 solar masses from Hellier et al. 2014, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of WASP-96 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.440.1982H/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 5540 +/- 140 K from Hellier et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-96 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.440.1982H/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Hellier et al. 2014, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of WASP-96 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.440.1982H/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/wasp-96.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.421, rounded to two decimals
spectralTypeSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-96 (pscomppars): spectral type G8, from Hellier et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.440.1982H/abstract)
objectTypeSource: SIMBAD, WASP-96: main object type *, Star
metallicitySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-96 (pscomppars): [Fe/H] 0.14 dex, from Hellier et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.440.1982H/abstract)
luminositySource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-96 (pscomppars): log10 of the luminosity in solar units 0.00217, from Wang et al. 2026 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2026AJ....171..147W/abstract)
ageSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-96 (pscomppars): age 8 Gyr, from Hellier et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.440.1982H/abstract)
rotationPeriodSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-96 (pscomppars): rotation period 20.16 d, from McGruder et al. 2023 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2023ApJ...944L..56M/abstract)
projectedRotationSpeedSource: NASA Exoplanet Archive, composite parameters of WASP-96 (pscomppars): projected rotation speed 1.5 km/s, from Hellier et al. 2014 (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2014MNRAS.440.1982H/abstract)
spinInclinationSource: Computed here from this record's rotation period, projected rotation speed and radius (1.05 solar radii): sin i = v sin i × P / (2πR) = 0.569. Not a measurement of the axis: the three numbers come from different papers.

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, colored from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
